thalamus.description: The thalamus is a large mass of gray matter located in the dorsal part of the diencephalon. It serves as a relay station for nearly all sensory information heading to the cerebral cortex.
thalamus.function: Acts as the brain's relay station, processing and transmitting sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex. Also plays a crucial role in regulating consciousness, sleep, and alertness.
thalamus.clinicalRelevance: Damage to the thalamus can result in sensory loss, movement disorders, and thalamic pain syndrome. Thalamic strokes can cause varied symptoms depending on the affected nuclei.
learningObjectives: Identify the location of the thalamus within the diencephalon
Describe the relay function of thalamic nuclei
Explain the role in sensory processing
Understand clinical implications of thalamic lesions
keyFacts: Processes all sensory information except smell

hippocampus.description: The hippocampus is a seahorse-shaped structure located in the medial temporal lobe. It is crucial for memory formation and spatial navigation.
hippocampus.function: Essential for forming new episodic memories, converting short-term memories to long-term storage, and spatial memory/navigation. Also involved in emotional responses.
hippocampus.clinicalRelevance: Early target in Alzheimer's disease, leading to memory impairment. Damage causes anterograde amnesia (inability to form new memories). Involved in temporal lobe epilepsy.
learningObjectives: Locate the hippocampus within the temporal lobe
Understand its role in memory consolidation
Describe the trisynaptic circuit
Recognize its involvement in Alzheimer's disease
keyFacts: Contains place cells for spatial navigation
Volume reduced in depression and PTSD

striatum.description: The striatum is the largest component of the basal ganglia, consisting of the caudate nucleus and putamen. It plays a critical role in motor control and reward processing.
striatum.function: Involved in motor planning, action selection, procedural learning, habit formation, and reward/motivation processing. Key component of motor and reward circuits.
striatum.clinicalRelevance: Dysfunction leads to movement disorders: Parkinson's disease (dopamine depletion), Huntington's disease (neuronal loss), and addiction disorders (reward pathway disruption).
learningObjectives: Identify caudate nucleus and putamen components
Understand role in basal ganglia circuits
Describe direct and indirect motor pathways
Explain involvement in movement disorders

ventricles.description: The ventricular system consists of four interconnected cavities within the brain filled with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). It includes two lateral ventricles, the third ventricle, and the fourth ventricle.
ventricles.function: Produces and circulates cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), provides cushioning for the brain, removes metabolic waste, and maintains intracranial pressure.
ventricles.clinicalRelevance: Hydrocephalus results from CSF accumulation. Ventricular enlargement seen in various conditions including schizophrenia, Alzheimer's disease, and normal pressure hydrocephalus.
learningObjectives: Trace CSF flow through ventricular system
Identify all four ventricles and connections
Understand CSF production and absorption
Recognize ventricular changes in disease

corpus_callosum.description: The corpus callosum is the largest white matter structure in the brain, consisting of over 200 million axons that connect the left and right cerebral hemispheres.
corpus_callosum.function: Enables interhemispheric communication, integrating motor, sensory, and cognitive information between brain hemispheres. Essential for unified perception and coordinated behavior.
corpus_callosum.clinicalRelevance: Agenesis causes developmental delays. Surgical section (corpus callosotomy) treats severe epilepsy. Damage can cause alien hand syndrome and disconnection syndromes.
learningObjectives: Identify anatomical divisions (genu, body, splenium)
Understand interhemispheric transfer
Describe effects of callosal section
Recognize developmental abnormalities
